study.notes: STUDY: STEP 1 (NCT03548935), 68 week double blind randomised placebo controlled phase 3 trial at 129 sites in 16 countries of once weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg (dose_mg 2.4) vs placebo, 2:1, plus lifestyle intervention, in adults without diabetes with BMI 30 or more, or 27 or more with a weight related condition; 1961 randomised (1306 and 655), treatment policy estimand at week 68; Table 2 (HTML table read from the NEJM page through the proxy, companion capture wilding2021_step1_nejm_tables1_2.txt) gives estimated mean changes per arm and the difference with 95 percent CI for systolic pressure (confirmatory secondary), diastolic pressure, HbA1c and fasting glucose (supportive secondary; route ci_95, MD) and ratios of the week 68 value to baseline with 95 percent CI for lipids and C-reactive protein (measure RR, log_RR_ci, ratio of geometric means convention); Table 1 baselines, lipid baselines are geometric means in mg/dL; pct_weight_change is the Table 2 coprimary difference in percent weight change, minus 12.44 (95 percent CI minus 13.37 to minus 11.51; arms minus 14.85 vs minus 2.41); funded by Novo Nordisk (industry_funded TRUE); rob_overall low

rows.notes: Table 2: change in systolic blood pressure from baseline to week 68 (confirmatory secondary), arms minus 6.16 vs minus 1.06 mm Hg, difference minus 5.10 (minus 6.34 to minus 3.87), P below 0.001; Table 1 baseline 126 and 127
Table 2: change in diastolic blood pressure from baseline to week 68, arms minus 2.83 vs minus 0.42 mm Hg, difference minus 2.41 (minus 3.25 to minus 1.57); Table 1 baseline 80 and 80
Table 2: change in glycated hemoglobin from baseline to week 68, percentage points, arms minus 0.45 vs minus 0.15, difference minus 0.29 (minus 0.32 to minus 0.26); Table 1 baseline 5.7 and 5.7

Table 2: change in fasting plasma glucose from baseline to week 68, mg/dl, arms minus 8.35 vs minus 0.48, difference minus 7.87 (minus 9.04 to minus 6.70); baseline glucose in the supplementary appendix, not captured
Table 2: total cholesterol ratio of week 68 value to baseline, arms 0.97 vs 1.00, treatment ratio 0.97 (0.95 to 0.98); Table 1 geometric mean baseline 189.6 and 192.1 mg/dL
Table 2: LDL cholesterol ratio of week 68 value to baseline, arms 0.97 vs 1.01, treatment ratio 0.96 (0.94 to 0.98); Table 1 geometric mean baseline 110.3 and 112.5 mg/dL
Table 2: triglycerides ratio of week 68 value to baseline, arms 0.78 vs 0.93, treatment ratio 0.84 (0.81 to 0.87); Table 1 geometric mean baseline 126.2 and 127.9 mg/dL

Table 2: C-reactive protein ratio of week 68 value to baseline, arms 0.47 vs 0.85, treatment ratio 0.56 (0.51 to 0.61); baseline CRP in the supplementary appendix, not captured; labelled C-reactive protein in the paper

json.design: STEP 1, multicentre double blind randomised placebo controlled phase 3 trial, semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly vs placebo 2:1, adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes, 1961 randomised, 68 weeks
json.reason: full text group (institutional route) with Tables 1 and 2 read as HTML from the NEJM page through the proxy; eight inventory markers: four as differences with 95 percent CI and four as ratios of the week 68 value to baseline with 95 percent CI
other_markers: HDL and VLDL cholesterol, free fatty acids ratios
waist circumference, BMI, body weight in kg

rob.justification: interactive web based randomisation with matching placebo and double blinding (D1, D2 low); treatment policy estimand with 94.3 percent completing the trial (D3 low); laboratory outcomes (D4 low); registered trial with a prespecified hierarchy of confirmatory and supportive secondary endpoints (D5 low)

doubts: lipid and CRP rows are treatment ratios of geometric means entered under measure RR by the existing pipeline convention
the companion abstracts and secondary STEP 1 analyses in the corpus (if any) must not be double counted against this primary report
